title: Troubleshoot Live activities | Adobe Journey Optimizer
t1: If profile is not found, the profile does not exist or ingestion is not completed Create the profile or wait for ingestion before triggering the Live activity.
t2: If profile is found, proceed to step 2 below to check if the push token is synced 2\ Check if Live activity push token is synced You can use Assurance to verify token registration.
t3: Verify the token configuration: { "liveActivityPushNotificationDetails": [ { "appId": "com.example.myapp", "token": "abc123def456...", "platform": "apns", "denylisted": false, "attributeType": "OrderTrackingAttributes", "identity": {} } ] } Validate each field: If any field is incorrect: Update the mobile app, re-register using Messaging.registerLiveActivities, wait 5-10 minutes, then re-check.
t4: If Adobe shows successful delivery but device does not show the Live activity: Check iOS device logs for Live activity errors Verify app is in foreground or background (not terminated).
t5: Subsequent API calls for update/end use this token for delivery Pre-checks: User Permission : The first time a Live activity starts on a device, iOS displays a system prompt: “Allow [App Name] to provide Live activity updates?” The user must tap “Allow” for update tokens to be generated and synced.
t6: Select the event and inspect the payload: Verify the token field contains a valid update token string Check the liveActivityID matches your Live activity instance.

title: Journey Agent Overview and User Guide | Adobe Journey Optimizer
t1: Event-triggered journey creation Create journeys that activate based on specific customer events Design automated responses to customer actions in real-time Build personalized communication flows based on customer behavior.
t2: Business-event triggered journey creation Create journeys that activate based on a particular business event and target a specified audience (e.g product back in stock or game score change) Build personalized communication flows based on customer behavior.
t3: Audience qualification journey creation Create journeys that activate as profiles enter or exit an audience segment definition Build personalized communication flows based on customer behavior.
t4: Conditional journey flows Create decision branches based on customer attributes Design split paths that adapt to customer preferences For each of these use cases, the agent translates natural language requirements into structured journey configurations.

title: Journey Orchestration - Frequently Asked Questions | Adobe Journey Optimizer

t3: Create two paths: If opened/clicked : Continue with next steps or end the journey Timeout path (not opened/clicked) : Send a reminder email with different subject line Best practice : Limit the number of resends to avoid appearing spammy (typically 1-2 reminders maximum).
t4: Create two paths : If Purchase event occurs : End the journey or continue with post-purchase flow Timeout path (no purchase) : Send an abandonment reminder email with cart contents.

t6: Create multiple paths based on criteria: Path 1 : High-value customers (total purchases > $1000) Path 2 : Regular customers (total purchases $100-$1000) Path 3 : New customers (total purchases < $100).

title: Landing Pages | Adobe Journey Optimizer B2B Edition
t1: In the _Create landing page_ dialog, enter a useful Name and Description (optional) Landing page requirements: Name - Maximum of 100 characters, must be unique, case-insensitive Description - Maximum of 300 characters Alpha, numeric, and special characters are allowed Reserved characters are _not allowed_ : \ / : ?.
t2: Drag and drop the HTML or .zip file containing your HTML content and click Import You can personalize the imported content as needed with the visual design space.
t3: From the _Landing pages_ listing page, click the landing page name to open it A preview of the visual content is displayed, with the landing page details on the right.
t4: To make changes to the content in the visual design space, click Edit landing page Use the visual design tools as needed: Add structure and content Add Assets Navigate the layers, settings, and styles Personalize content Edit linked URL tracking.
t5: From the _Landing page_ listing page, click the page name to open it A preview of the visual content is displayed, with the landing page details on the right.
t6: If you want to update the content, click Edit landing page on the right Click Create draft version in the dialog to open the draft version in the visual design space.

title: Migrate your default page load rule | Adobe Data Collection
t1: Select the rule that is your Analytics default load rule If you don’t know which rule is your default load rule, speak with someone who has a knowledge of the rules and what is in them.
t2: In order to migrate the current actions from the Analytics extension to the Web SDK extension, we need to know what variables are being set.
t3: At the top of the page, change the radio button to Provide JSON and you will be presented with a code view of the variables that are set.
t4: Cancel out of the Analytics Set Variables action so that you are back on the rule note important You have choices in this step, including the following.
t5: You can create a new action to send the data into Analytics via the Web SDK, leaving the Analytics action in place for now.
t6: Now change the radio button to Provide JSON or Data Element and paste the code that you copied in the previous step from Set Variables into this code window.

title: Set up Journey Optimizer web channel with Platform Web SDK | Adobe Data Collection
t1: Open the Journey Optimizer interface note Schema, datasets, and audiences can also be built in the Journey Optimizer interface as they are all common Experience Platform constructs.
t2: Add some additional details to the new web channel campaign First, name the campaign Call it Luma Loyalty Rewards – Gold Status Optionally, you can add a description to the campaign.
t3: In the browser tab with your Campaign, select the new LumaHomepage configuration note tip If the new configuration doesn’t appear in the dropdown, go to the Properties tab and then return to the Actions tab and check the dropdown again.
t4: Select Edit Content (or navigate to the Cotnent tab of the campaign) Since you entered a single page URL as the surface, you should be ready to begin working in the composer.
t5: In the Identity namespace field, select the namespace for identifying individuals within the chosen segment Since you are deploying the campaign on the Luma site, you can choose the ECID namespace.
t6: You can then log in to the site with various Luma loyalty accounts, and use the debugger to validate the requests sent to the Adobe Experience Platform Edge Network.

title: Implement Experience Cloud Integrations with tags | Adobe Data Collection
t1: Look in the row labeled “Supplemental Data ID.” The IDs from the first page load should match between Target and Analytics The IDs from the second page load should also match, but be different from the first page load.
t2: Set Customer Ids via the Id Service _before_ Target and Analytics fire their requests (which you accomplished using the rule ordering feature in tags).
t3: It should return you to the Homepage, which will also trigger a beacon that you can see in the Developer Tools If you are taken to the account info page, click on the WE.RETAIL logo to return to the homepage.

title: Simulate your journey | Adobe Journey Optimizer
t1: Click Create Simulated Users to create new users and select whether to create users from the UI or import them from JSON To reuse simulated users instead, click Select simulated users and choose entries you saved earlier.
t2: If you create simulated users from UI, enter a Display name and Description to identify this simulated user Then, select the attributes from the Union schema that you want to populate for this user.
t3: After you save, the simulated users you created appear in the Test users list For each entry, open the options menu and select one of the following: : Update the simulated user’s details.
t4: Click Send all to send every simulated users in the list into the journey A Simulated users have been sent successfully. confirmation message appears when the simulated users successfully enter the journey.
t5: Access the Results tab to open the execution log and review how each step ran After you validate the journey in Simulation , review the Results log.
t6: Once you have selected your simulated users, they are now available in the Test users list From the options menu, choose between the following option: to edit users and change its details.

title: Decisioning use case | Adobe Journey Optimizer
t1: Set the Priority of the decision item compared to others If a profile qualifies for multiple items, a higher priority grants the item precedence over others.
t2: Choose the ranking method to use to select the best offer for each profile In this case, select Offer priority : if multiple offers are eligible for this strategy, the Decisioning engine uses the value set as Priority in the offer(s).
t3: Choose the ranking method you want to use to select the best offer for each profile In this case, select Formula to use a specific calculated score to determine which eligible offer to deliver.
t4: Repeat steps 5 and 6 above to create another decision policy and select the second selection strategy that you created - the one with the formula as the ranking method.

title: Create a direct mail message | Adobe Journey Optimizer
t1: Provide basic information on your message (label, description, category), then choose the message configuration to use The configuration field is pre-filled, by default, with the last configuration used for that channel by the user.
t2: Once the content of the extraction file has been defined, you can use test profiles to preview it If you inserted personalized content, you can check how this content is displayed in the message, using test profile data.
t3: To define your target audience, click the Select audience button and choose from the available Adobe Experience Platform audiences note important For now, audience selection is restricted to 3 million profiles.
t4: Campaigns can be scheduled for a specific date or set to recur at regular intervals You can now start configuring the extraction file to send to your direct mail provider.
t5: Sometimes you may need to add information at the beginning or at the end of the extraction file To do this, use the Notes field then specify if you want to include the note as header or footer.
t6: To sort the extraction file using a column, select the column and toggle on the Sort by option The Sort By icon displays next to the column’s label in the Data Fields section.

title: Email Message Authoring | Adobe Journey Optimizer B2B Edition
t1: In the _Create email_ dialog, choose the type of email content that you want to author Use Themes \- Choose this option to create the email in _Theme mode_.
t2: Drag and drop the HTML or .zip file containing your HTML content and click Import You can personalize the imported content as needed with the visual email editor tools.
t3: To start your content design, drag an item from the Structures and drop it onto the canvas Add as many items from _Structures_ as you need and edit the settings for each in the pane on the right.
t4: To add conditional content and adapt the content to the targeted profiles based on conditional rules, select a content component and click the Enable conditional content icon in the component toolbar.
t5: In the _Styles_ tab that is displayed on the right, click Add custom CSS note The Add custom CSS button is available only when the _Body_ component is selected.
t6: To open the fragments listing, select the _Fragments_ icon ( ) You can: Sort the listing Browse, search, or filter the listing Switch between thumbnail and list views.

title: Migrate custom code to the Web SDK | Adobe Data Collection
t1: Scroll down to the Data Collection section and click to open the code window for onBeforeEventSend This is where you will paste any code that you want to run right before the event gets sent into Analytics from the Web SDK.
t2: For each of the plug-ins that you find in the new Web SDK plugins extension, remove the extension and the call to it from your code, and make sure that you then compensate for that removal by creating a data element and then calling that data element in the appropriate rule to set variables, etc.
t3: Next take a pass through your code to update or delete any old code that no longer applies to your analytics needs, as recommended at the top of this page.
t4: Last but certainly not least, test, test, and test some more After that, test again Make sure that your code is providing the results that you expect both in the Experience Platform debugger as well as in the reports in Adobe Analytics.

title: Troubleshooting guide for inbound actions in journeys | Adobe Journey Optimizer
t1: Scenario 1: The user hasn’t received the inbound content: In this scenario, a profile has entered the inbound action in the journey, but even after 30 minutes, the corresponding inbound content is not showing up in the device/client at the setup trigger step.
t2: Step 1: check if the device/client is receiving the content from the edge: Go to the Assurance session and select the In-App Messaging section from the left panel, in the Messages on Device tab, click the Messages drop-down list, look for a message with the journey name followed by ‘- In-app message’.
t3: Step 2: check if the edge network is returning the content: Open the Edge Delivery view in the Assurance session, verify if the Edge activity corresponding to the inbound action is listed in the Qualified Activities or Unqualified Activities sections.
t4: Step 3: check if the ‘joai’ audience membership has propagated to the edge: Navigate to the Customer > Profiles menu in the Journey Optimizer left navigation pane and browse to the profile using namespace and ID, select the Attributes tab and choose the Edge view, click View JSON to open the JSON view for the profile.
t5: Step 4: check if the ‘joai’ audience membership is present in the profile: Navigate to the Customer > Profiles menu in the Journey Optimizer left navigation pane and browse to the profile using namespace and ID, select the Attributes tab and choose the Hub view, click View JSON to open the JSON view for the profile.

title: Configure Sinch provider | Adobe Journey Optimizer
t1: In the left rail, browse to Administration > Channels > SMS Settings and select the API Credentials menu Click the Create new API credentials button.
t2: Click Verify SMS connection , from your existing API credentials, to test and verify your SMS API credentials by sending a sample message to a designated device.
t3: Fill in the Number and Message fields and click Verify connection note important The message must be structured to align with the provider’s payload format.
t4: Configure your MMS API credentials, as detailed below: SMS vendor : Sinch MMS Name : choose a name for your API Credential Project ID , App ID and API Token : follow the steps below to gather your MMS API credentials.
t5: To modify existing credentials, locate the desired API credentials and click the Edit option to make the necessary changes After creating and configuring your API credential, you now need to create your Webhook and a channel configuration for your RCS messages.

title: Personalization use case: cart abandonment email | Adobe Journey Optimizer
t1: Step 1: Create the initial event and the related journey: Create an event whose schema includes the productListItems array, define all the fields from this array as payload fields for this event, create a journey that starts with this event, add an Email activity to the journey.
t2: Step 2: Create the email: In the Email activity, click Edit content , then click Email Designer, from the left palette of the Email Designer home page, drag and drop three structure components onto the body of the message, drag and drop an HTML content component onto each new structure component.
t3: Step 3: Insert the customer’s first name in capital letters: On the Email Designer home page, click on the HTML component where you want to add the customer’s first name, on the contextual toolbar, click Show the source code, in the Edit HTML window, add the upperCase string function, in the left menu, select Helper functions.
t4: Step 4: Insert the list of items from the cart: Reopen the message content, on the Email Designer home page, click on the HTML component where you want to list the cart content, on the contextual toolbar, click Show the source code, in the Edit HTML window, add the each helper.
t5: Step 5: Insert a product-specific note: On the Email Designer home page, click on the HTML component where you want to insert the note, on the contextual toolbar, click Show the source code, in the Edit HTML window, add the if helper, in the left menu, select Helper functions, use the search field to find “if”.
t6: Step 6: Test and publish the journey: Turn on the Test toggle, then click Trigger an event, in the Event configuration window, enter the input values, then click Send, verify that there is no error, then publish the journey.

title: Delegate a subdomain | Adobe Journey Optimizer
t1: In the DNS record section, the list of records to be placed in your DNS servers is displayed Copy these records, either one by one, or by downloading a CSV file, then navigate to your domain hosting solution to generate the matching DNS records.
t2: Before submitting your subdomain setup, you have one more step to complete - click Continue Wait until Adobe verifies that the records are generated without errors on your hosting solution.
t3: You can create the records and submit the subdomain configuration later on using the Save as draft button note You will then be able to resume the subdomain delegation by opening it from the subdomains list.
t4: Before being able to use that subdomain to send messages, make sure that all DNS records are properly created, then wait until Adobe performs the required checks, which can take up to 3 hours.
t5: Pre-validate : Adobe checks whether the subdomain has been delegated to Adobe DNS (NS record, SOA record, Zone setup, ownership record) If the pre-validation step fails, an error is returned along with the corresponding reason, otherwise Adobe proceeds to the next step.
t6: Configure DNS for the domain : MX record : Mail eXchange record - Mail server record that processes inbound emails sent to the subdomain.

title: Customizable fragments | Adobe Journey Optimizer
t1: Click the Overview to check all the editable fields and their default values In this example, the button URL field displays with the default value defined in the component.
t2: Open your expression fragment, then edit its content in the personalization editor For HTML components, select the component in the fragment and click the Show the source code button.
t3: Replace render_content with the HTML code corresponding to the default rich content you want You can add bold, italic, line breaks, bulleted lists, etc.
t4: Create an email in a campaign or a journey, then add the fragment with rich text that was created You can see the two editable fields that were created on the right-hand side.

title: Configure a push notification | Adobe Journey Optimizer
t1: Open your journey then drag and drop an Action activity from the Actions section of the palette note important Legacy native channel activities (Email, Push, SMS, In-app, Web, Code-based experience, and Content Card) are deprecated as of the March 2026 release.
t2: Once your message content has been defined, you can use test profiles or sample input data uploaded from a CSV / JSON file, or added manually to preview its content.
t3: Select the type of campaign that you want to execute Scheduled - Marketing : execute the campaign immediately or on a specified date Scheduled campaigns are aimed at sending marketing messages.
t4: Click Create experiment to start configuring your content experiment and create treatments to measure their performance and identify the best option for your target audience.
t5: When your push is ready, complete the configuration of your campaign to send it To track the behavior of your recipients through push openings and/or interactions, make sure that the dedicated options in the tracking section are enabled in the campaign.

title: Set up an event forwarding with Platform Web SDK data | Adobe Data Collection
t1: Under the Environment ID dropdown, select the tag environment you are linking the event forwarding environment to, in this case Development note tip To send data to an event forwarding environment outside the Adobe org, select Manually enter IDs and paste in an ID.
t2: Select Save note caution Make sure to include the arc.event. prefix in the path Also, make sure to follow the exact case as the XDM Object field name—the ECID namespace must be in all caps.
t3: Search for the Adobe Cloud Connector , select Install There is no extension configuration needed With this extension, you can now forward data to a non-Adobe solution!.
t4: Lastly, validate the data matches in Webhook.site as well by viewing your open Webhook window Congratulations! You have configured event forwarding! Thank you for investing your time in learning about Adobe Experience Platform Web SDK.

title: Track event data in mobile apps with the Experience Platform Mobile SDK | Adobe Data Collection
t1: Navigate to Luma > Luma > Utils > MobileSDK in Xcode Project navigator, and add the following to the func sendCommerceExperienceEvent(commerceEventType: String, product: Product) function.
t2: For each of the buttons ( , , and ) in the toolbar, add the relevant call within the ATTrackingManager.trackingAuthorizationStatus == .authorized closure: 1.
t3: Navigate to Android > app > kotlin+java > com.adobe.luma.tutorial.android > models > MobileSDK in the Android Studio navigator, and add the following to the func sendCommerceExperienceEvent(commerceEventType: String, product: Product) function.
t4: Navigate to app > kotlin+java > com.adobe.luma.tutorial.android > views > ProductView.kt in the Android Studio navigator, and add various calls to the sendCommerceExperienceEvent function.
t5: At the LaunchedEffect(Unit) composable function, you want to send a product view event at the specific moment a product is viewed // Send productViews commerce experience event MobileSDK.shared.sendCommerceExperienceEvent("productViews", product).

title: Map identities | Adobe Experience Platform
t1: Select Create Now set up another namespace for the Luma Product Catalog Schema with the following details: Field Value Display name Luma Product SKU Identity symbol lumaProductSKU Type Non-people identifier.
t2: Press the Send button and you should get a 200 OK response: If you return to the user interface, you should now see your three new custom namespaces.
t3: Select Save Repeat this process to create a relationship between the Luma Web Events Schema and the Luma Product Catalog Schema Note that after defining the relationship, it is indicated in both the Composition and Structure section of the schema editor.

title: Create content cards | Adobe Journey Optimizer
t1: Open your journey, then drag and drop an Action activity from the Actions section of the palette note important Legacy native channel activities (Email, Push, SMS, In-app, Web, Code-based experience, and Content Card) are deprecated as of the March 2026 release.
t2: Select the type of campaign that you want to execute Scheduled - Marketing : execute the campaign immediately or on a specified date Scheduled campaigns are aimed at sending marketing messages.
t3: To test the content of your message, click Create experiment This allows you to test multiple variables of a delivery on sample populations to determine which treatment has the greatest impact on the targeted audience.
t4: Enable the Enable additional delivery rules option then select Edit rules to define when your message should be shown, dismissed, or permanently hidden Use rule builders to set specific conditions that trigger these actions.

title: Pause a journey | Adobe Journey Optimizer
t1: Select how to manage profiles which are currently in the journey However, a journey cannot remain paused indefinitely To prevent this, you can define how long the journey should stay paused (between 1 and 14 days).
t2: For single executions: No error will be shown at resume time if the scheduled date was before the resume date That schedule would be ignored.
t3: Select the …More button on the upper-right section of the journey canvas, and then Resume The journey switches to the Resuming status When the journey resumes, fresh entrances start within a minute.
t4: Profiles that were currently waiting in the journey on Action activities get resumed at a 5k tps rate They can then enter the Action they were waiting for, and continue the journey.

title: Attribute-based access control | Adobe Journey Optimizer
t1: From the Permissions product, select Role from the left pane menu and click Create role Note that you can also add Label to built-in roles.
t2: Select the Labels you want to add to your role and click Save For this example, grant the label C2 for users to access the previously restricted schema’s field.
t3: Select the corresponding Label , in this case, the C2 - Data cannot be exported to a third-party For the detailed list of available labels, refer to this page.
t4: Add a new Field group of your newly created Schema to the built-in Data source You can also create a new external data source and associated Field groups.
t5: Personalize your journey as needed, here we add an Email action If User Y, without access to label C2 objects, needs to access this journey with the restricted field: User Y will not be able to use the restricted field name since it will not be visible.

title: Landing Page Design | Adobe Journey Optimizer B2B Edition
t1: To start your content design, drag an item from the Structures and drop it onto the canvas Add as many items from _Structures_ as you need and edit the settings for each in the pane on the right.
t2: To add conditional content and adapt the content to the targeted profiles based on conditional rules, select a content component and click the Enable conditional content icon in the component toolbar.
t3: In the _Styles_ tab that is displayed on the right, click Add custom CSS note The Add custom CSS button is available only when the _Body_ component is selected.
t4: From the column toolbar, click the _Select a column_ tool and choose the one that you want to edit You can also select it from the structure tree.
t5: To edit the column properties, click the _Styles_ tab on the right and change them according to your needs: For Background , change the background color as needed.

title: Landing Page Template Design | Adobe Journey Optimizer B2B Edition
t1: To start your content design, drag an item from the Structures and drop it onto the canvas Add as many items from _Structures_ as you need and edit the settings for each in the pane on the right.
t2: To add conditional content and adapt the content to the targeted profiles based on conditional rules, select a content component and click the Enable conditional content icon in the component toolbar.
t3: In the _Styles_ tab that is displayed on the right, click Add custom CSS note The Add custom CSS button is available only when the _Body_ component is selected.
t4: From the column toolbar, click the _Select a column_ tool and choose the one that you want to edit You can also select it from the structure tree.
t5: To edit the column properties, click the _Styles_ tab on the right and change them according to your needs: For Background , change the background color as needed.

title: Core Extension Overview | Adobe Data Collection
t1: Configure when the page views are counted by selecting one of the following: Lifetime Current Session Sessions Trigger the action if the user’s number of sessions meets the specified criteria.
t2: Select whether the number of minutes the visitor is on the site must be greater than, equal to, or less than the specified value.
t3: Specify the number of pixels required for the screen resolution height Window Size Select the window size visitors must use on their devices for the action to be triggered.

title: Create an XDM schema for Platform Mobile SDK implementations | Adobe Data Collection
t1: In the Name and review step of the Create schema wizard, enter a Schema display name , for example Luma Mobile Event Schema and a Description, for example Schema for Luma mobile app experience events.
t2: Select Schemas under Data management to return to the main Schemas interface Keep in mind that you do not have to use all the fields in a group.
t3: This field is a container object for app interaction, so provide a camel-case Field name appInteraction, Display name App Interaction, and select Object from the Type list.
t4: To create an appStateDetails object containing a Measure field called screenView and two String fields called screenName and screenType, follow the same steps as you did when creating the appInteraction object.

title: Stream data to Adobe Experience Platform with Platform Web SDK | Adobe Data Collection
t1: Select Save As you generate traffic on the Luma demo website mapped to your tag property, the data populates the dataset in Experience Platform!.
t2: In the Debugger, open the “events” row to look for some of your XDM variables You have validated that data has left the browser and sent to the datastream!.
t3: In the Experience Platform interface, select Data Management > Datasets in the left-navigation to open the Datasets dashboard The dashboard lists all available datasets for your organization.
t4: Select your Luma Web Event Data dataset to open its Dataset activity screen The activity screen includes a graph visualizing the rate of messages being consumed as well as a list of successful and failed batches.
t5: From the Dataset activity screen, select Preview dataset near the top-right corner of your screen to preview up to 100 rows of data If the dataset is empty, the preview link is deactivated.
t6: First, run a query to see all of the names of the tables in the data lake Enter SHOW TABLES in the query editor and click the play icon to rn the query.

title: Validate Web SDK implementations with Experience Platform Debugger | Adobe Data Collection
t1: The Debugger will open and show some details of the hardcoded implementation (you may need to reload the Luma site after opening the Debugger).
t2: Confirm that the Debugger is “Connected to Luma ” as pictured below and then select the “lock ” icon to lock the Debugger to the Luma site.
t3: Select the Sign In button, sign into Adobe Experience Cloud using your Adobe Id, and select your Organization note tip If the debugger displays your username instead of your Org name after signing in, sign out and try again.
t4: Select your Development environment note tip If you are unable to select your property and environment using the dropdowns, instead go to Tags > Environments > Development > Install and select the icon to copy the embed code and paste it into the Debugger.
t5: Note how you can see the web.webPageDetails.pageView event type you specified in your Update variable action, and other, out-of-the-box variables adhering to the AEP Web SDK ExperienceEvent field group.
t6: Scroll down to the web object, select to open it and inspect the webPageDetails.name They should match the corresponding adobeDataLayer data layer variables on the homepage To view and compare the adobeDataLayer data layer on the homepage.

title: Configure permissions | Adobe Experience Platform
t1: Name the role Luma Tutorial Platform (add the tutorial participant’s name to the end, if multiple people from your company are taking this tutorial) and select Confirm.
t2: After adding all of the permission items, be sure to select the Save button You will make a few small updates to this role after the Create a sandbox and Set up Developer Console and Postman lessons.
t3: Add a new profile named Luma Tutorial Data Collection (add the tutorial participant’s name to the end, if multiple people from your company are taking this tutorial).
t4: Add the tutorial participant as an admin of this profile After completing these steps, you should see that the Luma Tutorial Data Collection profile is set up with one admin.
t5: Complete the workflow to add yourself as a user to the product profile You do not need to add yourself as a Developer for Data Collection.

title: AEP Audience Activation Fails Due to List Limit in Adobe Campaign Managed Cloud | Adobe Experience Platform
t1: Open the Audience Job Audit for the failing audience and verify the following: 1 A Create audience job failed with: _NMS-470323 Maximum audience list size limit of< limit> reached._ 2.
t2: Save the change and inform your team that the affected audience must run through a new Create/Load cycle after this change to create the missing list.
t3: In AEP, perform one of the following actions for the affected audience: 1 Deactivate and re-activate the audience for the Adobe Campaign Managed Cloud destination, or 2.

title: Enable External Integrations | Adobe Journey Optimizer
t1: Navigate to the Configurations section in the left menu and click Manage from the Integrations card Then, click Create Integration to start a new configuration.
t2: Configure the Path Template with Name and Default value for every placeholder you added in the URL Note that the Name is a marketer-facing label in the editor only, it is not sent on the API request.
t3: Click Add Header and/or Add Query Parameters as needed for your integration For each parameter, provide the following details: Parameter : The actual header or query parameter name as expected by the API.
t4: Choose an Authentication Type : No Authentication : For open APIs that do not require any credentials API key : Authenticate requests using a static API key.
t5: Set Policy configuration such as Timeout period for API requests and choose to enable throttling, cache and/or retry note With throttling enabled, supported rates are 50 to 5000 TPS.
t6: With the Response payload field, you can decide which fields of the sample output needs to be used for message personalization Click the icon and paste a sample JSON response payload to automatically detect data types.

title: Create a WhatsApp message | Adobe Journey Optimizer
t1: In the Business rules section, you can apply a rule set to control communication pressure on WhatsApp messages You can now start designing the content of your WhatsApp message from the Edit content button, as detailed below.
t2: Click Create experiment to start configuring your content experiment and create treatments to measure their performance and identify the best option for your target audience.
t3: From the Action triggers menu, choose the Frequency of your WhatsApp message: Once Daily Weekly Month You can now start designing the content of your WhatsApp message from the Edit content button, as detailed below.
t4: In the Image URL field, add media URLs to replace any placeholders in your template Meta’s template media are only placeholders To display images, audio, or video correctly, you must use external URLs from Adobe Experience Manager or other sources.
t5: Use the personalization editor to add personalization to your template You can use any attribute, such as the profile name or city for example.

title: Engage customers by browsing activity | Adobe Journey Optimizer
t1: Click Add attribute to create following three attributes: Wishlist > description Wishlist > priceref Wishlist > imageurl This enriches the message with detailed wishlist information.
t2: Create a new audience for retargeting based on engagement with emails Here we create an audience based on email click events, to retarget all of the people who interacted with a previously sent email, and more specifically, clicked on a link within that message.
t3: Create the message content for each channel including profile attributes, such as the recipient’s name, along with enrichment data like Wishlist items, to personalize each message.

title: Direct mail configuration | Adobe Journey Optimizer
t1: In the save dialog, select All files (_._) as the file type to ensure the key is saved as plain text and not as a .ppk file.
t2: Open the saved file with a text editor and verify its format: The file must start with --BEGIN RSA PRIVATE KEY -- (five dashes before and after).
t3: Enter a name and a description (optional) for the configuration, then select the channel to configure note Names must begin with a letter (A-Z).
t4: Select Marketing action(s) to associate consent policies to the messages using this configuration All consent policies associated with the marketing action are leveraged in order to respect the preferences of your customers.
t5: Select the File routing configuration amongst the ones that you created This defines where the file will be exported for your direct mail provider to use.

title: Forms | Adobe Journey Optimizer B2B Edition
t1: In the _Create form_ dialog, enter a useful Name (required) and Description (optional) Form requirements: Name - Maximum of 100 characters, must be unique, case-insensitive Description - Maximum of 300 characters Alpha, numeric, and special characters are allowed Reserved characters are _not allowed_ : \ / : ?.
t2: From the _Forms_ list page, click the form name to open it A preview of the form content is displayed, with the form details on the right.
t3: To make changes to the form in the visual design space, click Edit form Use the visual design tools as needed: Add fields Change field styling Reorder fields Change submit button text and styling Change the form styling Click Save & close to return to the form details.
t4: When the form meets your criteria and you want to make it available for use in a landing page or landing page template, click Publish.
t5: Use the visual design tools as needed to update the form content: Add fields Change field styling Reorder fields Change submit button text and styling Change the form styling Click Save & close to return to the form details.

title: SMS Authoring | Adobe Journey Optimizer B2B Edition
t1: Click the _Personalize_ icon ( ) to the right of the text message box The dialog provides access to the account tokens, person tokens, and system tokens.
t2: Add a token by clicking the plus ( + ) symbol next to it If you want to add the token with a fallback (default that appears in case that field is not available for a lead), click the _More_ icon ( … ) and choose Insert with fallback text.
t3: When your personalization tokens are placed, click Save to save changes and return to the main SMS authoring workspace You can continue to edit the message with the tokens as needed.
t4: If you choose to use a Marketo Engage landing page, set the tracking options Enable tracking \- Select this checkbox to enable tracking, which requires _shortening_ the URL.
t5: In the _SMS properties_ section, enter a Name (required, 100 character maximum) and Description (optional, 300 character maximum) for your message Alpha, numeric, special characters are allowed for these fields.

title: CMK Alert Resolution Reference | Adobe Experience Platform
t1: Alert categories categories: The following sections outline the types of alerts that may be triggered by Customer Managed Key (CMK) issues in Adobe Experience Platform: Key access disabled Key access failure Alert notification.
t2: Key access disabled: This alert indicates that Adobe Experience Platform is unable to access the configured CMK because the key is disabled or inaccessible due to its configuration, in such cases, the system treats the condition as an intentional removal of key access.
t3: When it occurs: This alert is triggered when the encryption key in Azure Key Vault is in a disabled state, deleted, or misconfigured in a way that prevents access during platform operations.
t4: Possible causes: The following are common reasons this alert may occur: The key was manually disabled, key operations (wrapKey/unwrapKey) have been removed, the key activation date is set in the future, the key expiration date is in the past, the key has been deleted.
t5: Resolution: Navigate to the Azure Key Vault that contains the CMK, select the key associated with Adobe Experience Platform, verify that the key’s status is set to Enabled, if the key is disabled, enable it using the Azure portal or the CLI command az keyvault key enable, re-add the wrapKey and unwrapKey permissions to the key.
t6: Key access failure: This alert indicates that Adobe Experience Platform failed to access the CMK due to network-level or configuration-based denial of access, this is treated as a recoverable error, data is not purged under SLA in this case.
t7: When it occurs: This alert is typically triggered when the Key Vault firewall is not configured to allow Adobe CMK access or when identity-based access fails.
t8: Resolution: Verify that the Key Vault and encryption key still exist, if the key was deleted, follow the soft-delete recovery steps under “Key access disabled.” If MultiTenant App permissions are missing or changed, confirm that the Adobe MultiTenant App has the following permissions: get, wrapKey, and unwrapKey on the key.
t9: Alert notification: This alert serves as a general notification for CMK configuration or access anomalies that don’t match a known failure type, this alert may reflect an internal error, a novel misconfiguration, or an unexpected condition.

title: Single-Page Applications | Adobe Journey Optimizer B2B Edition
t1: Understanding SPAs: Unlike traditional multi-page websites where each navigation triggers a full page load, SPAs use JavaScript to update content dynamically while maintaining a single HTML page, this approach creates several considerations for web experiences: No page reloads \- Content changes occur without triggering traditional page load events.
t2: Configure SPA support: To personalize SPAs effectively, you need to configure view tracking so that Journey Optimizer B2B Edition can identify when users navigate between virtual views.
t3: Set up view declarations: Work with your development team to implement view declarations using the Adobe Web SDK, using these view declarations involve calling the sendEvent command with view information whenever the SPA navigates to a new view.
t4: Target specific views: In the web channel configuration, set up URL matching rules that align with your SPA routing structure, when creating modifications, specify the view where the modification should apply, use CSS selectors that target elements specific to each view.
t5: Handle dynamic content: In the non-visual editor, add a modification with a CSS selector, enable Wait for element and specify the maximum wait time, the modification applies once the target element appears in the DOM.
t6: SPA frameworks: Journey Optimizer B2B Edition web experiences work with popular SPA frameworks: Framework Considerations React Modifications apply after React renders components to the DOM, use class names or data attributes for targeting, angular Target elements after Angular’s change detection runs, avoid targeting elements with ngIf before they render.
t7: Use stable selectors: SPAs often generate dynamic class names or IDs (especially with CSS-in-JS solutions), as an alternative, you can use: Data attributes \- Add custom data attributes (data-testid, data-section, etc.) to elements you want to target, semantic HTML \- Target based on HTML structure and semantic elements.
t8: Test views: Navigate through all views where modifications apply, test the full user flow, including: Direct navigation to a view (deep linking) Navigation from other views within the SPA Browser backward and forward navigation, verify that modifications reapply when returning to a previously visited view.
t9: Handle view transitions: Some SPAs use animations or transitions between views, consider: Timing \- Ensure modifications apply after transition animations complete, element visibility \- Elements may exist but be hidden during transitions, flickering \- Apply modifications early enough to avoid visible content changes.
t10: Troubleshooting: Check view tracking \- Verify that sendEvent calls include the correct view name, verify element existence \- Ensure that target elements are in the DOM when modifications apply, review selectors \- Confirm CSS selectors match the actual DOM structure, check console \- Look for JavaScript errors that might prevent modifications.

t3: Guardrails: To help you build a journey without running into errors, the following guard rails are in place: _Deleting a Split path node_ : Deleting a node requires deleting all subsequent nodes in each path, _Deleting a Merge node_ : A merge node can be deleted only when there is one path connected to it.
t4: Add a node: Navigate to the journey map, click the plus ( + ) icon on the path and select the node type, set the node properties on the right.
t5: Delete a node: Navigate to the journey map, in the node properties on the right, click the _Delete_ ( ) icon, in the conformation dialog, click Delete.
t6: Add and delete a path: Navigate to the journey map, click the plus ( + ) icon on the path and add the split path node, in the node properties on the right, select Account, to add more paths, click Add path.
t7: Schedule a journey: Navigate to the journey map, schedule your journey by clicking Journey settings in the header, in the dialog, set the schedule options: Choose a schedule type, click Save.
t8: Publish a journey: At the top right of the journey map, click Publish, in the _Review journey settings_ dialog, set the journey start options, if needed, specify the End date for the journey, click Next, in the confirmation dialog, click Publish.

title: Getting started with the Web SDK tag extension | Adobe Data Collection
t1: (Optional) You can add more fields or field groups for any additional data that you want to collect Once saved, schemas only allow _additive_ changes.
t2: Under the Datastreams section, select the desired datastream for each environment All other configuration settings are either filled out for you or optional Set any desired configuration settings, then select Save.
t3: Set the following properties on the right: Variable type : XDM Sandbox : The sandbox that you created your schema in Schema : The desired schema.
t4: Install the embed code within a test web page on your site Once you validate that the tag works on your devlopment environment, you can use the Publishing flow interface to publish the library to staging, then eventually to production.

t2: Navigate to Luma > Luma > Views > General > DisclaimerView in Xcode’s Project navigator The Xode’s Project navigator is the view that is shown after installing or reinstalling the application and starting the app for the first time.

title: Using External Integrations | Adobe Journey Optimizer
t1: Navigate to the Integrations section and click Open integrations to view all active integrations Note that Journey Optimizer Fragments are available with Integrations but support outbound channels only.
t2: When you author integration personalization, the Integrations helper includes a required field that defines how failures or missing data interact with default content: required=true (default): Rendering stops for that message.
t3: To complete your integration setup, define your integration attributes, which were previously specified during configuration You can assign values to these attributes using either static values, which remain constant, or profile attributes, which dynamically pull information from user profiles.
t4: (Optional) Open the Helper function menu and add a helper, for example, the Let function, if you want to bind a named variable to the reservation response.
t5: If you use a helper variable, map that variable to the field the reservation integration returns for downstream use, for example, the flight number in the passenger or booking payload.

title: Configuration steps | Adobe Journey Optimizer
t1: Select Upload DDL file to define an entity relationship diagram and create schemas The table structure must contain: At least one primary key A version identifier, such as a lastmodified field of type datetime or number.
t2: Set up each schema and its columns, ensuring that a primary key and a version descriptor are specified One attribute, such as lastmodified, must be designated as the version descriptor (type datetime, long, or int) to ensure datasets are updated with the latest data.
t3: Click the button next to the Source Join, then drag and guide the arrow towards the Target Join to establish the connection note Composite keys spanning multiple fields are supported when defined in the DDL file.
t4: Fill in the given form to define the link and click Apply once configured Cardinality : 1-N : one occurrence of the source table can have several corresponding occurrences of the target table, but one occurrence of the target table can have at most one corresponding occurrence of the source table.
t5: All links defined in your data model are represented as arrows in the canvas view Click on an arrow between two tables to view details, make edits, or remove the link as needed.
t6: Click Open Jobs to monitor the progress of the creation job This process may take couple minutes, depending on the number of tables defined in the DDL file.

title: Configure Twilio provider | Adobe Journey Optimizer
t1: In the left rail, browse to Administration > Channels > SMS Settings and select the API Credentials menu Click the Create new API credentials button.
t2: Configure your SMS API credentials, as detailed below: SMS vendor : Twilio Name : choose a name for your API Credential Account SID and Auth Token : access the Account Info pane of your Twilio Console Dashboard page to find your credentials.
t3: Click Verify SMS connection , from your existing API credentials, to test and verify your SMS API credentials by sending a sample message to a designated device.
t4: Fill in the Number and Message fields and click Verify connection note important The message must be structured to align with the provider’s payload format.
t5: Create an SMS Webhook Configure an SMS Webhook that can receive incoming RCS message responses or delivery updates This webhook must be properly linked to your Twilio setup for two-way communication.
t6: Create API Credential using Custom as SMS vendor In Journey Optimizer, define new API credentials specifically for RCS using “Custom” as the SMS vendor.

title: Configure your custom provider | Adobe Journey Optimizer
t1: In the left rail, navigate to Administration > Channels , select the API Credentials menu under SMS settings , and click the Create new API credentials button.
t2: Configure your SMS API credentials, as detailed below: SMS vendor : Custom Name : Enter a name for your API Credential Provider AppId : Enter the application ID provided by your SMS provider.
t3: Enable the mTLS support option, which ensures that both the client and server authenticate each other before establishing a secure connection To use mTLS only, select No Authentication from the Auth Type drop- down and then enable mTLS support.
t4: In the Headers section, click Add new parameter to specify the HTTP headers for the request message that will be sent to the external service.
t5: Add your Provider Payload to validate and customize your request payloads For RCS messages, this payload is later used during content design note When configuring a custom SMS provider with Basic or Bearer authentication, you must include the authOption parameter in the JSON payload.

title: Set up channel configurations | Adobe Journey Optimizer
t1: Enter a name and a description (optional) for the configuration, then select the channel to configure note Names must begin with a letter (A-Z).
t2: Select Marketing action(s) to associate consent policies to the messages using this configuration All consent policies associated with the marketing action are leveraged in order to respect the preferences of your customers.
t3: Once all the parameters have been configured, click Submit to confirm You can also save the channel configuration as draft and resume its configuration later on.
t4: Once the channel configuration has been created, it displays in the list with the Processing status During this step, several checks will be performed to verify that it has been configured properly.

title: Dynamic media | Adobe Journey Optimizer
t1: In the Edit HTML menu, navigate to Assets then click Open asset selector Alternatively, you can copy and paste the URL of your asset.
t2: Update the images parameters: Layer : enter the base element where your text is placed Size : update the size of your text block.
t3: In the Image settings , navigate to access the parameters of your dynamic media template The available fields depend on the parameters added during the template creation in Adobe Experience Manager.
t4: Fill in the different fields and use the personalization editor to add personalized content You can use any attribute, such as the profile name, city, or other relevant details, to create a more customized experience.

title: Use supplemental identifiers in journeys | Adobe Journey Optimizer
t1: Access the event schema and locate the attribute you want to use as a supplemental identifier (e.g., booking ID, subscription ID) and mark it as an ID.
t2: Use the expression editor to select the attribute you marked as the supplemental ID note Make sure you are using the expression editor in Advanced mode to select the attribute.

t5: In the Supplement identifier field, use the expression editor to select the attribute you marked as the supplemental ID note Make sure you are using the expression editor in Advanced mode to select the attribute.

title: Use visual fragments | Adobe Journey Optimizer
t1: Drag and drop any fragment from the list into the area where you want to insert it note caution You can add any Draft or Live fragment to your content.
t2: Select the fragment to display the corresponding pane on the right From there, you can delete the fragment from your content, or duplicate it.
t3: From the Settings tab, you can: Choose the devices you want the fragment to be displayed on Open the fragment in a new tab to edit it if needed.

title: Set quiet hours | Adobe Journey Optimizer
t1: In the Time zone drop-down, apply a standard time zone to all recipients in the audience, regardless of their individual time zones To use the time zone field from each profile, select Use recipients local time zone.
t2: Specify the time period at which quiet hours should apply Weekly \- Choose specific days of the week and a timeslot You can also enforce the rule All day.
t3: In the Handling actions during quiet hours section, choose how messages are treated during the selected period of time: Queue message \- Messages are sent at the completion of the quiet hours period unless in Paused state.
t4: Click the Add Business Rule button and select the rule set containing the Quiet hours rule note Only activated rule sets display in the list.

title: Build your first rule | Adobe Journey Optimizer
t1: Add a condition conditions: Access the rule builder from a Build audience activity, click the Add condition button to create a first condition for your query, identify the attribute from the dabatase to use as criteria for your condition, click Confirm to add the selected attribute to your condition.
t2: Custom conditions on linked tables (1-1 and 1-N links) links: Navigate inside the Brand table and select the Label attribute, define the expected value for the attribute, select the Purchases table and confirm, clic Add condition to define the sub-conditions to apply to the selected table, add sub-conditions to suit your needs.

title: Brand alignment | Adobe Journey Optimizer

title: Manage brand | Adobe Journey Optimizer

title: Manage web modifications | Adobe Journey Optimizer
t1: Select an unwanted modification and click the Delete modification option from the More actions button to remove it note caution Proceed with care when deleting an action as it may impact subsequent actions.

title: Lesson 4 - Create a push campaign | Adobe Journey Optimizer
t1: On the next screen, depending on the mobile device you have, select either the iOS™ or Android™ tab to configure your content iOS Android 4.2.3.1 Compose Message section.

title: Use Brand Themes for Email Content | Adobe Journey Optimizer B2B Edition

title: Adobe Target External Audiences | Adobe Journey Optimizer B2B Edition
t1: From the node properties on the right, set the external audience If there are one or more external audiences already created, you can choose Select existing and select the audience that you want to use.

title: Configure top and bottom of page events in Web SDK | Adobe Data Collection
t1: Create an XDM object (or Variable) data element that populates _experience.decisioning.propositions with each rendered proposition’s id, scope, and scopeDetails, and sets _experience.decisioning.propositionEventType.display to 1.

title: Create data elements for Platform Web SDK | Adobe Data Collection
t1: Learning objectives: At the end of this lesson, you are able to: Understand different approaches to mapping a data layer to XDM Create data elements to capture data Map data elements to an XDM object.
t2: Data layer approaches: Implement XDM in the data layer, map to XDM in tags, map to XDM in the datastream The examples in this tutorial follow the Map to XDM in tags approach.
t3: Implement XDM in the data layer: In this approach, web developers implement a fully-defined XDM object as the structure for the data layer, then you simply map the entire data layer to an XDM object in tags.
t4: Map to XDM in tags: This approach involves mapping individual data layer variables to data elements in tags and eventually to XDM, this is the traditional approach to implementation using a tag management system.
t5: Map to XDM in the datastream: This approach uses functionality built-into the datastream configuration called Data Prep for Data Collection and skips mapping data layer variables to XDM in tags.
t6: Create data elements to capture the data layer: Go to Data Elements and select Add Data Element (or Create New Data Element if there are no existing data elements in the tag property), name the data element Page Name, use the JavaScript Variable Data Element type to point to the value in Luma’s data layer: adobeDataLayer.0.page.name.
t7: Create Variable data elements for XDM and data objects: Select Add Data element, name your Data Element XDM Variable, select the Adobe Experience Platform Web SDK as the Extension, select the Variable as the Data Element Type, select XDM as the property, select the Sandbox in which you created the schema.

title: Connections overview | Adobe Real-Time Customer Data Platform
t1: The brands create accounts in Collaboration if they haven’t already, being sure to select the appropriate role type (advertiser or publisher) Once the prerequisites are met, the connection process can begin.

title: Engage and acquire new customers without dependency on third-party cookies | Adobe Real-Time Customer Data Platform
t1: How to achieve the use case: high-level overview: As a customer , you license prospect profiles from one or more data partners to help drive top of the funnel customer acquisition, as a customer , you extend your profile data and governance model to ingest the partner -provided list of prospect profiles.
t2: License third-party profile details from the partner: from-partner This step is covered in the prerequisites and Adobe assumes that you have the right contractual agreements in place with trusted data vendors to ingest prospect profiles provided by the data partner.

t4: Load the list of prospect profiles and inspect the prospect profiles view: Navigate to Data Management > Datasets and select Create dataset, select Create dataset from schema, select the schema that you created in a previous step, give your dataset a name and optionally a description, select Finish.

t6: Activate prospect profiles to destinations: Make use of the prospect audiences by exporting them to destinations, currently, only certain cloud storage destinations support activation of prospect profiles, read more about activating prospects to cloud storage destinations.

title: AI Assistant for Personalization Expressions | Adobe Journey Optimizer
t1: In the text field, describe the personalization expression you want in plain language — for example which profile attributes, segments, or logic you need, then click Generate.

title: Journey capping & arbitration | Adobe Journey Optimizer

title: Error codes reference | Adobe Journey Optimizer
t1: CJMPTS: Push and transport service errors: These errors occur during push notification delivery and message transport operations, error Code Description Root Cause Resolution CJMPTS-1410-500 Internal server error on push/channel send action Channel backend outage, expired credentials, misconfiguration, or provider bug 1\, retry after delay 2\, check provider configurations and quotas 3\.
t2: CJMMAS: message authoring service errors: These errors occur when creating, editing, or publishing messages, presets, and content, error Code Description Root Cause Resolution CJMMAS-1732-500 Proof has failed - All assets not published when sending proof/test with AEM asset Recently published asset isn’t in AJO yet; asset ID mismatch; cross-repo use; AEM sync lag 1\.
t3: CJMCMP: Campaign errors: These errors occur during campaign creation, configuration, and activation, error Code Description Root Cause Resolution CJMCMP-6003-400 “There is at least one incorrect campaign” when publishing/test mode journey/message Node references a missing, unpublished, or invalid campaign; legacy or cloned journey not creating inlines 1\, open each message node and verify configuration 2\.
t4: CJMTL: transport layer errors: These errors occur during message transport and delivery operations, error Code Description Root Cause Resolution CJMTL-010018-422 “Personalization not allowed in domain name” when saving/sending content Overly strict validation temporarily broke dynamic href domain personalization 1\, refactor links if using domain variables 2\, verify the latest AJO version is in use 3\.
t5: CJMRPS: reporting and provisioning service errors: These errors occur during reporting configuration and dataset provisioning operations, error Code Description Root Cause Resolution CJMRPS-1047-409 “Conflict, dataset has been added already” when adding reporting dataset Attempting to add a dataset which is already provisioned 1\, review dataset configuration in reporting settings 2\.
t6: Before journey activation: Validate all resources : Ensure all referenced audiences, events, data sources, and custom actions are properly configured Test thoroughly : Use test mode to identify issues before publishing (.

t1: Test across devices and clients \- Verify email rendering on popular email clients (Gmail, Outlook, Apple Mail) and devices (desktop, mobile, tablet) to ensure consistent display (email channel only).

t4: Use seed lists for stakeholder monitoring \- Configure seed lists to automatically include internal stakeholders who will receive copies of all deliveries at execution time for quality monitoring and compliance verification (email channel only).
t5: Simulate journey paths \- For complex journeys with multiple branches, use test mode to test different entry conditions and profile attributes to validate all possible paths.
t6: Document test results \- Keep records of test outcomes, issues found, and resolutions to improve future testing processes and share learnings with your team.

t4: Click Trigger an event , select your event, and enter a test profile identifier (for example, the email address of a profile flagged as a test profile in Adobe Experience Platform).

t6: When all steps show finished and no errors are logged, deactivate test mode and publish the journey If the profile does not appear in the log at all, check that: The profile identifier you entered is flagged as a test profile in Adobe Experience Platform.
