t2: Deep link connect: Select this option to generate a unique session URL, QR code, and PIN, scan the QR code or manually open the session link in your app, then enter the PIN to establish the connection, select Deep link connect and proceed by selecting Start.
t3: Quick connect: Trigger the Assurance connection \- In your mobile app or implementation, trigger the action that initiates the Assurance connection using the startSession API, select and connect your device \- Once your device appears in the list of available devices, select it and click Connect.
t4: Deep link connect sessions: Navigate to your session details page (for existing sessions) or proceed from session creation to see the link, QR code, and PIN, use your device’s camera app to scan the QR code, or copy the link and open it in your app.
t5: Quick connect sessions: Navigate to your session details page (for existing sessions) or proceed from session creation, in the Connect Device section, you’ll see the device picker interface, trigger the action set in your app to make the device discoverable, select your device from the list and click Connect.
t6: Verifying Connection: You can verify that your app is connected to Assurance when the Adobe Experience Platform icon (red Adobe “A”) is displayed on your app.
t7: Export a session: To export an Assurance session, on your app’s sessions details page, select Export to JSON in a session: The export option respects search filter results and only exports events displayed in the event view.

title: Capillary Streaming Events Overview | Adobe Experience Platform
t1: In the create schema dialog, pick between Manual creation (Add fields and field groups yourself) or ML-assisted creation (Upload a CSV file and use machine learning to generate a recommended schema).
t2: Choose a base class for your schema (e.g., XDM Individual Profile, XDM ExperienceEvent, or Other) If you select Other , you can select from available custom or standard classes.
t3: Use the Schema Editor to: Add field groups (reusable blocks of fields), define individual fields (customize names, data types, and options), and optionally, create custom data types or field groups if existing ones do not fit your needs.
t4: (Optional) Edit fields, add descriptions, and adjust field groups as needed in the Schema Editor For a detailed instructions on how to create an XDM schema, read the guide on creating a schema using the schema editor.

title: Bot Filtering Using Statistics and Machine Learning | Adobe Experience Platform
t1: Specify the model name (bot_filtering_model) to indicate which model to evaluate This name must match the one you created earlier with the CREATE MODEL command.
t2: Include the evaluation dataset to define the dataset for evaluation Ensure the dataset includes the same feature columns (count_per_id, web, id) and the label column (isBot) used during training.
t3: To supply the correct data for predictions, use a SELECT statement to specify the feature columns (count_per_id, web, id) Do not include the label column (isBot) because the model will generate predictions for this field.

title: SQL Insights | Adobe Experience Platform
t1: Ad hoc query exploration: Begin by executing ad hoc SELECT queries to explore raw data on the data lake This allows for on-the-fly, exploratory data analysis to experiment, and validates data where the results of the queries are not stored in the data lake.
t2: Batch query utilization: Use batch queries to create scheduled jobs for generating insights aggregate tables, ensuring a systematic and automated approach to data processing.
t3: Aggregated insights loading: Load the generated aggregated insights into the accelerated store and use SQL to test queries, and ensure the accuracy and efficiency of data retrieval.
t4: Access and integration: Access the insights stored in the accelerated store seamlessly by integrating with Adobe Experience Platform User-defined Dashboards or other preferred Business Intelligence (BI) tools.

title: Apply the data governance framework | Adobe Experience Platform
t1: Go to the Labels tab to see all labels in the account There are many out-of-the-box labels, plus you can create your own via the Create label button.
t2: You can either apply labels to individual fields or apply them to the entire dataset We will apply the label to the entire dataset.
t3: Select the policy and then enable it via the Policy status toggle You can create your own policies by selecting the Create policy button.

title: Query Service in Jupyter Notebook | Adobe Experience Platform
t1: In Experience Platform, navigate to Notebooks from the left navigation column Allow a moment for JupyterLab to load note note If a new Launcher tab did not automatically appear, open a new Launcher tab by clicking File then select New Launcher.
t2: In the Launcher tab, click the Blank icon in a Python 3 environment to open an empty notebook note note Python 3 is currently the only supported environment for Query Service in notebooks.
t3: Find an Adobe Analytics dataset to explore and right-click on the listing, click Query Data in Notebook to generate SQL queries in the empty notebook.
t4: Click the first generated cell containing the function qs_connect() and execute it by clicking the play button This function creates a connection between your notebook instance and the Query Service.
t5: Copy, paste, and execute the following import statements in a new cell These statements will be used to visualize your data: import plotly.plotly as py import plotly.graph_objs as go from plotly.offline import iplot.
t6: Next, copy and paste the following variables in a new cell Modify their values as needed, then execute them target_table = "your Adobe Analytics dataset name" target_year = "2019" target_month = "04" target_day = "01" target_table: Name of your Adobe Analytics dataset.

title: Trigger an Orchestrated campaign using a signal | Adobe Journey Optimizer
t1: Define each parameter’s name and data type to send in the signal payload You can also provide Test values that will be used when you trigger the campaign in test mode.
t2: If you’ve defined parameters in the signal, you can wire them into your canvas logic (for example, in conditions or targeting) In this example, the “channel” parameter is used as a condition in a Test activity.
t3: Open the campaign scheduler, select Copy API request and choose the format (cURL or HTTP Request) The copied information includes the orchestrated campaign ID, sandbox name, organization ID, and test values for your parameters if you have added some.
t4: Send the trigger API call using the sample request you have copied from the scheduler See Trigger Orchestrated campaigns API for request and response details.

title: Add a channel activity in a multistep campaign | Adobe Journey Optimizer
t1: In the right rail, use the Category field to choose Marketing or Transactional for this message Transactional messages do not require opt-in and are suited for time-sensitive communications such as disruptions, emergencies, or cancellations.
t2: Select a channel configuration A configuration is defined by a System Administrator It contains all the technical parameters for sending the message, such as header parameters, subdomain, mobile apps, etc.
t3: Apply capping rules In the Rule set drop-down list, select a channel rule set to apply capping rules to your campaign Leveraging channel rule sets allows you to set frequency capping by communication type to prevent overloading customers with similar messages.
t4: Create a content experiment Use the Content experiment section to define multiple delivery treatments in order to measure which one performs best for your target audience.
t5: Add multilingual content Use the Languages section to create content in multiple languages within your campaign To do so, click the Add languages button and select the desired Language settings.
t6: Select an outbound channel activity in the canvas and click Edit email , Edit SMS , or Edit Push depending on the chosen channel.

title: Build rules | Adobe Journey Optimizer
t1: If you create a Decision item rule, you can select Enable dataset lookup to use data from Adobe Experience Platform to enrich your decision logic with external data.
t2: Build the rule to suit your needs using the Adobe Experience Platform Segment Builder To do this, you can leverage various data sources such as: Profile attributes; Decision item attributes - only available when creating a Decision item rule; Audiences; Context data coming from Adobe Experience Platform.
t3: To validate that both expressions behave identically, click Download Optimisation Analysis (TSV) to download a file showing how simulated profiles are evaluated against each version.

title: Configure the SMS configuration | Adobe Journey Optimizer
t1: Enter a name and a description (optional) for the configuration, then select the SMS channel note Names must begin with a letter (A-Z) It can only contain alpha-numeric characters.
t2: If you want to use the URL shortening function in your SMS messages, select an item from the Subdomain list note To be able to select a subdomain, make sure you have previously configured at least one SMS/MMS subdomain.
t3: In the Execution dimension section, use the SMS Execution Field to select amongst the profile attributes the phone number that you want to use in priority if several numbers are available in the database.
t4: Once all the parameters have been configured, click Submit to confirm You can also save the channel configuration as draft and resume its configuration later on.
t5: Once the checks are successful, the channel configuration gets the Active status It is ready to be used to deliver messages You are now ready to send text messages with Journey Optimizer.

title: Personalize email configuration settings | Adobe Journey Optimizer
t1: Add dynamic subdomains: Before creating a configuration, set up the subdomains you want to use for sending emails according to your use case, create a channel configuration, select the Email channel, in the Subdomain section, enable the Dynamic Subdomain option, select the Edit icon next to the first Condition field, the personalization editor opens.
t2: Personalize your header: Define your header parameters as you would usually do, for each field, select the Edit icon, the personalization editor opens, repeat the steps above for each parameter you want to add personalization to.
t3: Use personalized URL tracking: Go to the URL tracking parameters section of your email channel configuration, click the Edit icon next to each field, select the profile attribute of your choice from the personalization editor, repeat the steps above for each tracking parameter you want to personalize.
t4: View configuration details: Create an email campaign or journey, select the Edit content button, click the View configuration details button, the Delivery settings window displays, select Expand to display the dynamic subdomains’ details.
t5: Check your configuration: From the edit content screen of your message or in the Email Designer, click the Simulate content button, select a test profile, if an error is displayed, click the View configuration details button, check the Delivery settings screen for the errror details.

title: Notify users about product availability | Adobe Journey Optimizer
t1: After starting draft mode, preview the audience with Wishlist details For deeper insights, click an output result and select Preview results Here, the data displays both recipients and their Wishlist items.
t2: To be able to send a separate email for each item, make sure that your email configuration is set with Recipients - email as Profile Target Dimension and Wishlistitems as a Secondary dimension.
t3: Once your campaign is tested and ready, click Publish to make it live With this orchestrated campaign, customer receives a separate email for each of their wishlist items.

title: Use Adobe Experience Platform data for decisioning | Adobe Journey Optimizer
t1: Click Select dataset to display all Adobe Experience Platform datasets that have been enabled for lookup Select the dataset with the attributes you need.
t2: Click Select key to choose a joining key (e.g., flight number or customer ID) that exists in both the decision item attributes and the dataset.
t3: When defining the item eligibility, click Add dataset and select the appropriate dataset note If the dataset you are looking for does not display in the list, make sure you have enabled it for lookup and you have created a dataset lookup mapping.
t4: Select the In total capping type then enable the Expression option note If the dataset you are looking for does not display in the list, make sure you have enabled it for lookup and you have created a dataset lookup mapping.

title: Adobe Analytics integration | Adobe Journey Optimizer
t1: Configure Adobe Analytics or Web SDK data: Browse to the Sources menu, in the Adobe Analytics section, select Add data, from the list of available Adobe Analytics report suites, select the Report suite to enable, choose if you want to use a Default or Custom schema, from the Dataflow detail screen, choose a Dataflow name.
t2: Activate this configuration: Get the data source ID, contact Adobe Customer Care with the following details: Subject: Enable Adobe Analytics events for journeys Content: Please enable my environment to use AA events, once you have a confirmation that your environment is ready, you can use Adobe Analytics data in your journeys.
t3: Create a journey with an event using Adobe Analytics or Web SDK data: From Adobe Journey Optimizer, access the Configuration menu, then, select Manage from the Events card, click Create event, fill in the Event parameters: Name : Personalize the name of your Event, when configured, select Save.

title: Get started with journeys & campaigns approval | Adobe Journey Optimizer
t1: Approval policies setup An admin user creates an approval policy, defining conditions under which the policy should apply to journeys or campaigns For example, you can create an approval policy that requires all scheduled campaigns created by a given user to be approved before activation.
t2: Campaign/journey submission for approval The campaign/journey creators build a journey or campaign and submit it for approval The campaign/journey enters an “In Review” state, during which no edits can be made unless the request is canceled.
t3: Review and approval The approver(s) defined in the approval policy that applies to the journey or campaign receive(s) a notification They can review the journey or campaign content, audience, and settings.

title: Browse and filter your journeys | Adobe Journey Optimizer
t1: Journeys calendar calendar: To access the calendar view, open the journeys list and click the icon, use the arrow buttons or the date selector above the calendar to move between weeks, click the icon to toggle the display of items that span multiple days or weeks.
t2: Journey statuses: The journey status depends on its lifecycle, it can be: Draft : the journey is in its first stage, it has not been published yet, draft (Test) : the test mode has been activated using the Test mode button.
t3: Duplicate a journey: Navigate to the journey you want to copy, click the More actions icon (the three dots next to the journey name), select Duplicate, enter the name of the journey and confirm, the new journey is created and available in the journey list.
t4: Bulk operations: From the list of your journeys, you can pause multiple Live journeys, to pause a group of journeys (_bulk pause_), select them in the list and click the Pause button in the blue bar at the bottom of the screen, the Pause button is only available when Live journeys are selected.

title: Batch decisioning | Adobe Journey Optimizer
t1: Get started with batch decisioning start: Journey Optimizer allows you to deliver offer decisions to all profiles in a given Adobe Experience Platform audience, to do this, you need to create a job request in Journey Optimizer that will contain information on the audience to target and the offer decision to use.
t2: Create a job request: In the Offers menu, open the Batch decisioning tab then click Create request, name your job request, then select the dataset where the job data should be sent into, select the Adobe Experience Platform audience to target.
t3: Monitor batch jobs: All requested batch jobs are accessible from the Batch decisioning tab, additionally, search and filtering tools are available to help you refine the list.
t4: Duplicate a job request duplicate: You can reuse information of an existing job to create a new request, to do this, click the duplicate icon, edit the job information if necessary, then click Create to create the new request.

title: Configure subdomains for text messages (SMS/MMS) | Adobe Journey Optimizer
t1: Enter the prefix that will display in your SMS URL Only alpha-numeric characters and hyphens are allowed note caution Do not use cdn or data prefixes as these are reserved for internal use.
t2: Once submitted, the subdomain displays in the list with the Processing status For more on subdomains’ statuses, refer to this section Before being able to use that subdomain to send messages, you must wait until Adobe performs the required checks, which can take up to 4 hours.
t3: The record to be placed in your DNS servers displays Copy this record, or download a CSV file, then navigate to your domain-hosting solution to generate the matching DNS record.
t4: Make sure that DNS record has been generated into your domain-hosting solution If everything is configured properly, check the box “I confirm…”, then click Submit.

title: Create a fragment | Adobe Journey Optimizer
t1: Define the fragment’s properties properties: Access the fragment list through the Content Management > Fragments left menu, select Create fragment and fill in the fragment name and description (if needed), select or create Adobe Experience Platform tags from the Tags field to categorize your fragment for improved search.
t2: Design the fragment content content: After you have configured the fragment’s properties, the Email Designer or the personalization editor opens, depending on the type of fragment you are creating, contextual attributes are not supported within fragments.
t3: Preview and publish the fragment publish: Go back to the fragment creation screen after designing its content, or open it from the list of fragments, a preview of the fragment is available under the Tags field, allowing to check its rendering, click the Publish button in the upper-right corner to publish the fragment.

title: Manage users and roles | Adobe Journey Optimizer
t1: Type in your user’s name or email address or select the user from the list, and click Save If the user was not previously created in the Admin Console, refer to the Add users documentation.
t2: The Resources menu displays the list of resources that apply to the Experience Cloud - Platform powered applications product Drag and drop resources to assign permissions.
t3: Select from the different resources such as Journeys , Segments , or Decision management available in Journey Optimizer listed in the left-hand menu Here we select the Journeys resource.
t4: From the Journeys drop-down, select the permissions to assign to your Role Here we select View journeys , View journeys report and View journeys event, data sources, actions.

title: Create code-based experiences | Adobe Journey Optimizer
t1: Drag and drop an Action activity from the Actions section of the palette note important Legacy native channel activities (Email, Push, SMS, In-app, Web, Code-based experience, and Content Card) are deprecated as of the March 2026 release.
t2: Select the Edit content button and edit your content as desired using the personalization editor Note that the templates available to choose are scoped to either HTML or JSON based on the channel configuration that has been chosen beforehand.
t3: From the journey activity or the campaign edition screen, select Edit code note If you are using a code-based experience content template with predefined editable form fields, you can manage the content of these fields without opening the personalization editor.

title: Journey Optimizer Experimentation Accelerator | Adobe Journey Optimizer
t1: Enter the user’s name, email address, or choose from the list, then click Save If the user was not previously created, refer to this documentation.
t2: Add the permissions this profile should have, such as View Experiments and Manage Experiment Metadata , then click Save note tip Create separate profiles when users need different access levels.
t3: Add the users who should receive this access, then click Save Users added to this profile can now access Journey Optimizer Experimentation Accelerator from the app switcher.

title: Buying Group Role Templates | Adobe Journey Optimizer B2B Edition
t1: To filter the list by name, use the search field at the top of the list Enter the first few characters of the name to reduce the displayed list to the matching items.
t2: Click Add Condition and define the conditional rule for the role In the _Condition_ dialog, expand the list of Person attributes and locate an attribute that you want to use to match the role.
t3: For each additional role that you want to include for the template, click Add another role and repeat steps 1 and 2 to define the role.
t4: In the dialog, change the Members required value for each defined role as needed You can enter the value, or click + or − to increase or decrease the value.

title: Account Lists | Adobe Journey Optimizer B2B Edition
t1: In the _Add accounts by filter_ dialog, use the Account Filters menu to add the attributes and activities that you want to use to construct the filter set: The filters are nested into category folders.
t2: When the filter set and logic are complete, click Populate accounts The population process may take some time, depending on the number of accounts to evaluate and populate (the size of your database and the filter criteria you selected).
t3: In the _Publish static account list_ dialog, click Publish to confirm Dynamic account list You can proceed to publish a dynamic account list as soon as the filter set is complete.

title: Configure Engagement Score Weighting | Adobe Journey Optimizer B2B Edition
t1: Click Engagement score weighting on the intermediate panel to display the list of scoring models From this page, you can create (duplicate), activate, and edit engagement score models.
t2: In the _Duplicate_ dialog, enter a unique name for the duplicated model and click Duplicate Click the name to open the score model details and make your changes.
t3: For each weight band, adjust the name or values according to your needs: Change the name in the _Weighting band_ field Enter a new value.
t4: If needed, add another weighting band: Click \+ Add weighting band at the bottom of the list This action inserts a blank weighting band at the bottom of the list.

title: Snapchat Conversions API extension overview | Adobe Data Collection
t1: From the drop-down menu, select the appropriate item, and fill in the Path field in the right-side panel to reference the desired data in your schema.
t2: Name the rule and configure a condition for triggering the Snap event For example, to send a PURCHASE event whenever an event includes an order number, set a condition to check if the user interaction contains a valid purchase order number.
t3: After saving the condition, add an action to trigger the Snap Conversion API In the left-side panel: Set the Extension dropdown menu to Snap Conversions API Extension.
t4: Configure the CAPI parameter values you want to send for the event in the Data Bindings section on the right-side panel The fields in the extension map to CAPI parameters as shown below.

title: Collect analytics and apply personalization in ChatGPT Apps (MCP data collection) | Adobe Data Collection
t1: Architecture: MCP host (ChatGPT) : ChatGPT invokes tools exposed by your MCP server and provides a stable pseudonymous user identifier in request metadata, mCP server (backend) : Owned by your organization, adobe IMS : Issues access tokens used by your MCP server to call Adobe data collection APIs.
t2: Data flow: User prompts ChatGPT using your MCP server, chatGPT interprets the prompt’s intent and calls the appropriate backend MCP tool, backend MCP server uses the Data Collection APIs (interact endpoint) to send an experience event to the Edge Network for analytics collection and optional personalization.
t3: Validation: Once all of the above steps are configured, you can validate the following: Data collection: Verify that events are reaching the desired dataset and that each event is processed as expected, personalization: Verify that decisions are returned by the Edge Network, and that those decisions are rendered by your widget.
t4: Security and privacy considerations: Treat ChatGPT’s identifiers as sensitive, even though they are pseudonymous, make sure that you apply your organization’s consent and data governance practices to this workflow, adobe recommends using OAuth 2.1 workflows for authorization, ensure that access tokens and secrets never reach the client or UI.

title: Libraries | Adobe Data Collection
t1: Create a library: Open the Publishing tab, select Add New Library, name the library, assign the library to a Dev environment, add a change to the library, to add any resources that have changed, select Add All Changed Resources, select Save or Save and Build for Development.
t2: Add to a library: Install the extensions you want to add, create the data elements and rules you want to add, open the Publishing tab, select the library you want to change, then select Edit, use the rules, data elements, and extensions buttons to select the items you want to add to the library.
t3: Remove from a library: Disable the extensions you want to remove, along with any data elements and rules that depend on those extensions, disable the data elements and rules you want to remove, open the Publishing tab, select the library you want to change.
t4: Manage library changes: Choose a library and select Edit to view library changes, select a change to view and select a revision, select whether to show All items or Changed items, select the revision, then select Select Revision, select either Add a Change or Add All Changed Resources.
t5: Active Library: Create a new library, go to Rules, Data Elements, or Extensions, select your Active Library, make your changes, then save and build the library, test your changes, and repeat these steps as needed.

title: Incremental Load in Query Service | Adobe Experience Platform
t1: Create a checkpoint_log table to track the most recent snapshot used to process data successfully The tracking table (checkpoint_log in this example) must first be initialized to null in order to incrementally process a dataset.
t2: Populate the checkpoint_log table with one empty record for the dataset that needs incremental processing DIM_TABLE_ABC is the dataset to be processed in the example below.
t3: Set the from_snapshot_id which indicates where the processing starts from The from_snapshot_id in the example is queried from the checkpoint_log table for use with DIM_TABLE_ABC.
t4: Set the to_snapshot_id as the current snapshot ID of the source table (DIM_TABLE_ABC) In the example, this is queried from the metadata table of the source table.
t5: Use the CREATE keyword to create DIM_TABLE_ABC_Incremenal as the destination table The destination table persists the processed data from the source dataset (DIM_TABLE_ABC) This allows the processed data from the source table between from_snapshot_id and to_snapshot_id, to be incrementally appended to the destination table.

title: Salesforce CRM connection | Adobe Experience Platform
t1: In the Select source field window, choose the Select attributes category and select the XDM attribute or choose the Select identity namespace and select an identity.
t2: In the Select target field window, choose the Select identity namespace and select an identity or choose Select custom attributes category and select an attribute or define one using the Attribute name field as needed.
t3: Finally, go to the Salesforce website and validate if the profiles from the audience have been updated Working with Contacts If you have selected _Contacts_ within your Experience Platform segment, navigate to the Apps > Contacts page.

title: Process Customer Consent Data Using the Adobe Experience Platform Web SDK | Adobe Experience Platform
t1: Set up a datastream: In order for the SDK to send data to Experience Platform, you must first configure a datastream, in the Data Collection UI or Experience Platform UI, select Datastreams in the left navigation.
t2: Install and configure the Experience Platform Web SDK: Once you have created a datastream as described in the previous section, you must then configure the Experience Platform Web SDK extension that you will ultimately deploy on your site.
t3: Create a data element to set default consent: Determine the user’s region on the web server, before the script tag (embed code) on the web page, render a separate script tag that sets an adobeDefaultConsent variable based on the user’s region.
t4: Deploy the extension on your website: Once you have finished configuring the extension, it can be integrated into your website, refer to the publishing guide in the tags documentation for detailed information on how to deploy your updated library build.

title: IAB TCF 2.0 Support in Experience Platform | Adobe Experience Platform
t1: Determine how to generate customer consent data within your CMP: Since each CMP system is unique, you must determine the best way to allow your customers to provide consent as they interact with your service, a cookie consent dialog is a common way to attain customer consent, an example CMP dialog is seen below.
t2: Consent strings: Regardless of the method you use to collect the data, the goal is to generate a string value based on the consent options chosen by the customer, called a consent string.
t3: Create datasets with TCF consent fields datasets: Customer consent data must be sent to datasets whose schemas contain TCF consent fields, refer to the tutorial on creating datasets for capturing TCF 2.0 consent for how to create the required profile dataset (and an optional Experience Event dataset) before continuing with this guide.
t4: Update Profile merge policies to include consent data: Once you have created a Profile-enabled dataset for collecting consent data, you must ensure that your merge policies have been configured to always include TCF consent fields in your customer profiles, this involves setting dataset precedence so that your consent dataset is prioritized over other potentially conflicting datasets.
t5: Integrate the Experience Platform Web SDK to collect customer consent data: sdk The use of the Experience Platform Web SDK is required to process consent data directly in Adobe Experience Platform, experience Cloud Identity Service is not supported.
t6: Create a datastream: In order for the SDK to send data to Experience Platform, you must first create a datastream for Experience Platform, specific steps for how to create a datastream are provided in the SDK documentation, after providing a unique name for the datastream, select the toggle button next to Adobe Experience Platform.
t7: Test your implementation: Once you have configured your TCF 2.0 implementation and have exported segments to destinations, any data that does not meet consent requirements will not be exported.

title: Learn how to author and share your own Playbooks using the AI Assistant. | Adobe Experience Platform
t1: Log into the source organization : Navigate to the organization that contains the playbook you created and want to share from the Your playbooks tab.
t2: Publish the playbook : If the playbook isn’t already published, you must publish it before sharing note note A partnership must be established between the source and target organizations to enable playbook sharing.
t3: Import the playbook : Select Import to bring the playbook into the target organization You can view it in the Playbooks tab If the playbook doesn’t appear, ensure it is published and that the organization partnernship is active.

title: Data warehouse connection | Adobe Experience Platform
t1: Steps: Browse to the FEDERATED DATA section on the left rail, in the Federated Databases link, click on the Add federated database button, add a name and select Snowflake, fill in the details, click on the Test connection button, and then on the Deploy functions button.
t2: Steps: In the FEDERATED DATA section, click Models, browse the Schema tab and click on the Create Schema button, select your source database in the list, and click on the Add tables tab, choose the tables from the federated source.
t3: Create a Data Model: Data models allow you to create a link between tables, the link can be created between tables in the same database, such as tables in Snowflake, or between tables in different databases, such as a link between a table in Snowflake and a table in Amazon Redshift.

title: Delete destinations | Adobe Experience Platform
t1: Go to the Experience Platform UI and select Destinations from the left navigation bar Select Browse from the top header to view your existing destinations.
t2: Select the filter icon on the top left to launch the sort panel The sort panel provides a list of all your destinations You can select more than one destination from the list to see a filtered selection of dataflows associated with the selected destination.
t3: Select the name of the destination that you want to delete If the destination has existing dataflows, you are taken to the Dataflow runs tab.
t4: Select Delete in the confirmation dialog to remove the destination Depending on server load, it can take a few minutes for Experience Platform to delete the destination.

title: Activate audience data to streaming destinations | Adobe Experience Platform
t1: Select your destination: Go to Connections > Destinations , and select the Catalog tab, select Activate audiences on the card corresponding to the destination where you want to activate your audiences, as shown in the image below, select the destination connection that you want to use to activate your audiences, then select Next.
t2: Select your audiences: To select the audiences that you want to activate to the destination, use the checkboxes to the left of the audience names, then select Next, you can select from multiple types of audiences, depending on their origin: Segmentation Service : Audiences generated within Experience Platform by the Segmentation Service, for more details.
t3: Map attributes and identities mapping: In the Mapping page, select Add new mapping, select the arrow to the right of the Source field entry, in the Select source field page, use the Select attributes or the Select identity namespace options to switch between the two categories of available source fields.
t4: Apply transformation: When you are mapping unhashed source attributes to target attributes that the destination expects to be hashed (for example: email_lc_sha256 or phone_sha256), check the Apply transformation option to have Adobe Experience Platform automatically hash the source attributes on activation.
t5: Schedule audience export scheduling: On the Audience schedule page, select each audience, then use the Start date and End date selectors to configure the time interval for sending data to your destination, select Next to go to the Review page.
t6: Review review: On the Review page, you can see a summary of your selection, select Cancel to break up the flow, Back to modify your settings, or Finish to confirm your selection and start sending data to the destination.
t7: Consent policy evaluation: If your organization purchased Adobe Healthcare Shield or Adobe Privacy & Security Shield, select View applicable consent policies to see which consent policies are applied and how many profiles are included in the activation as a result of them, read about consent policy evaluation for more information.
t8: Data usage policy checks: In the Review step, Experience Platform also checks for any data usage policy violations, shown below is an example where a policy is violated, you cannot complete the audience activation workflow until you have resolved the violation.
t9: Filter audiences: Also in this step you can use the available filters on the page to display only the audiences whose schedule or mapping has been updated as part of this workflow, you can also toggle which table columns you want to see.

title: How unified and enriched Profiles fuels data activation with Real-Time CDP
t1: Test with real use cases: Apply a few representative use cases to each approach to determine which one most effectively addresses your key objectives.
t2: Google Audience Match If you identify audience segments—such as users who prefer to book on weekdays, weekends, or specific days of the week—you can activate them in Adobe Target to personalize their booking experience.
t3: An enriched profile with unified view to know and understand the customers better These superheroes are in charge now to do wonders Adopting Adobe Real-Time CDP is a game-changer for businesses seeking to deliver personalized customer experiences.

title: Start and monitor Orchestrated campaigns with Adobe Journey Optimizer | Adobe Journey Optimizer
t1: Campaign lifecycle at a glance lifecycle: Orchestrated campaigns move through a defined set of states, the key stages in the publication workflow are: Status What it means Draft The campaign is being built and tested — not yet active, live The campaign has been published and is executing.
t2: Test your campaign before publishing test: Journey Optimizer allows you to test Orchestrated campaigns before going live, when a campaign is created, it enters the Draft state by default, in this state, you can execute the campaign manually to test the flow, all activities in the canvas are executed except Save audience activities and channel activities.
t3: Publish the campaign publish: Once your campaign is tested and ready, click Publish to make it live, all errors must be fixed before being able to publish a campaign, the visual flow restarts, and real profiles begin flowing through the journey in real-time.
t4: Publication-time execution sequence: Scheduler activation — If the campaign has a schedule configured, the scheduler kicks in and triggers execution at the defined time, save Audience activities run first — Any Save audience activities in the workflow execute before message activities.
t5: Confirm message sending: By default, for non-recurring orchestrated campaigns, message delivery is paused until you explicitly approve the send, after publishing the campaign, confirm the send request from the channel activity’s properties pane, until it is confirmed, the channel activity stays pending and no message is sent.
t6: Activity execution indicators activities: This may involve confirming the sending of a delivery or taking a necessary action, to resolve the issue, open the Orchestrated campaign logs.
t7: Logs and tasks: Monitoring logs and tasks is a key step to analyze your Orchestrated campaigns and make sure they are running properly, logs and tasks are accessible from the Logs button which is available in both test and live mode in the canvas toolbar, the Tasks tab details the step-by-step execution sequence of activities.

title: Add personalization | Adobe Journey Optimizer
t1: Where can I add personalization where: You can add personalization in Journey Optimizer in every fields with the icon, expand the sections below for more details, messages In messages, personalization can be added at different locations in your messages, such as the Subject line field, it can also be added in other sections of your content.
t2: Personalization sources sources: The navigation pane lets you select the source for personalization, available sources are: Profile attributes : lists all the references associated to the profile schema described in Adobe Experience Platform Data Model (XDM) documentation, target attributes : This folder is specific to Orchestrated campaigns, it contains attributes calculated directly within the campaign canvas.
t3: Add personalization add: The central workspace is where you build your personalization syntax, to use an attribute to personalize your message, locate it into the left navigation pane and click the + button to add it into the expression.
t4: Validation mechanisms: The validation of your expression is automatically executed when you click on the Add button to close the editor window, you can also use the Validate button to check your personalization syntax, expand the section below to see common errors that may occur when validating personalization.

title: Track your messages | Adobe Journey Optimizer
t1: Choose the type of link you want to create: Select External link to insert a link to an external URL Select Landing page to insert a link to a landing page.
t2: Enter the desired URL in the corresponding field, or select a landing page, and define the link settings and styles When trying to send the proof or email, if you are returned an error involving a URL added to your content, you can URL encode the string as a workaround.

title: Journey Optimizer Get Started for System Admin | Adobe Journey Optimizer
t1: Set up access and permissions: Create sandboxes to partition your instances into separate, isolated virtual environments, understand roles, set permissions for roles, including Sandboxes , and give access to your team members by assigning them to different roles, use object-level access control (optional).
t2: Configure channels and messages: Set up channel configurations, delegate subdomains : for any new subdomain to be used in Journey Optimizer, the first step will be to delegate it, create IP pools : improve your email deliverability and reputation by grouping together IP addresses provisioned with your instance.

t4: Collaborate across roles: Your administrative work enables all teams to succeed: Support Data Engineers Collaborate with Data Engineers on data management and access, review the Get started with data management overview to understand the schemas, datasets, and data sources your data engineers need to configure.

title: Decision items | Adobe Journey Optimizer
t1: Set the Priority of the decision item compared to others, if a profile qualifies for multiple items A higher priority grants the item precedence over others.
t2: Use fragments to add multiple contents to the decision item - for example, if you want to display different contents for several mobile device models.

title: Web channel prerequisites | Adobe Journey Optimizer
t1: Implementation prerequisites: Two types of implementations are supported to enable authoring and delivery of web channel campaigns on your web properties: Client-side only – To add modifications to your website, you need to implement the Adobe Experience Platform Web SDK on your website.
t2: Visual authoring prerequisites: To be able to open, author and preview your web pages reliably into the Journey Optimizer web designer, you must have the Adobe Experience Cloud Visual Editing Helper browser extension installed on your web browser, google Chrome and Microsoft Edge are currently the only browsers that support authoring web pages in Journey Optimizer.
t3: Install the visual editing helper extension: Open a new tab in your browser (Google Chrome or Microsoft Edge), go to the Google Chrome Web Store, if you are using Microsoft Edge, select Allow extensions from other stores on the top banner, search and navigate to the Adobe Experience Cloud Visual Editing Helper browser extension.
t4: Reporting prerequisites: To enable reporting for the web channel, you need to make sure the dataset used in your web implementation datastream is also included in your reporting configuration, in other words, when configuring reporting, if you add a dataset that is not present in your web datastream, web data will not display in your reports.
t5: Branded domains for assets: When authoring web experiences, if you add content coming from the Adobe Experience Manager Assets library, you must set up the subdomain that will be used to publish this content.

title: Design Inbox | Adobe Journey Optimizer
t1: Select an inbox layout: List layout : shows each content card in a vertical list so profiles can scroll through messages and open them one at a time.

title: Create dynamic content | Adobe Journey Optimizer
t1: Select the Conditions menu to display the list of available conditional rules Click the + button next to a rule to add it into the current expression.

title: Form Design | Adobe Journey Optimizer B2B Edition
t1: Fields: Form fields are used to capture person profile data that can be used to target people and associate them with accounts and buying groups.

t9: CSS styles: Click View CSS in the right panel to review the CSS code, select the CSS code in the scrolling window and copy it to your clipboard, click Close, (Optional) Paste the copied code into your favorite CSS tool and edit the CSS to reflect the styling that you want.
t10: Manual styling: Change the settings in the right panel to define the display for the whole form, background color \- Select the checkbox to apply a background color around the form area, white is the default color, click the color square to open the popup color picker and choose a color for the form background.
